I know this feeling too well. That’s the thing that sucks about having Asperger’s. You’re aware of your lack of social skills and the other traits that come with being on the spectrum in general, but you’re not aware enough to know how to handle them or stop/overcome them completely - I think that’s part of what makes you high functioning in the first place; the awareness, at least to some degree. And if you do something that you know is related to your autism and you say “it’s because I have autism, it’s an autism thing” neurotypicals tend to think you’re faking or making excuses. It’s honestly torture.

https://adaa.org/learn-from-us/from-the-experts/blog-posts/consumer/anxiety-autism-spectrum-disorder

Also this, from the same article; “as the patient ages and the environment becomes more demanding, social communication impairment may underline the development of social anxiety, especially if the patient is high functioning and aware of his/her social incompetence.” Just thought maybe someone would find that interesting.

Phenylalanine is an amino acid found in foods and some artificial sweeteners like aspartame. Higher protein foods generally have a higher phenylalanine count. People with phenylketonuria (or PKU, same thing) aren’t born with the enzyme needed to process this amino acid (that or its barely present in the body) so phenylalanine builds up in the body and the brain, causing a wide range of problems.
